Analyst Commentary Recent price target moves around Andritz give a sense of how bullish analysts are thinking about the stock right now. Targets in the €87 to €90 range set a reference point for how they see the balance between current valuation and future execution. Bullish Takeaways Bullish analysts highlight that price targets clustered between €87 and €90 imply confidence that Andritz can support a higher valuation multiple than before, based on their updated assumptions. The revised targets indicate that analysts see room for Andritz to meet revenue and profit margin assumptions that they consider achievable under their current models. The use of higher fair value estimates suggests that bullish analysts see the current share price as not fully reflecting their view of Andritz's medium term earnings power. Retention of positive ratings, including an Overweight stance from JPMorgan, shows that some major institutions remain comfortable with Andritz's risk and reward profile at these levels. Bearish Takeaways Even with higher targets, some cautious analysts may see Andritz as closer to what they view as fair value. This can limit potential upside if execution on revenue and margin assumptions falls short. Target ranges that are relatively tight, such as €87 to €90, leave less room for error on factors such as discount rate assumptions, P/E expectations and earnings delivery. Any shift in broader Street assumptions, such as a lower accepted P/E for the sector, could reduce the implied valuation support behind these updated targets. Investors relying on these targets need to recognise that they rest on specific model inputs. Any disappointment versus the assumed growth or profitability path for Andritz could put pressure on the shares. What’s in the News for Andritz Andritz and RAG Austria have started construction on Austria's largest green hydrogen facility, a 12.5 MW solar powered electrolyzer designed to convert surplus renewable electricity into about 17,000,000 cubic meters of green hydrogen annually, with planned start of operations by the end of 2026. Source: company announcement summarized in recent news coverage. The green hydrogen project is intended to support seasonal energy storage, energy security and industrial decarbonization efforts in Europe, with Andritz responsible for engineering, procurement and construction. Source: recent news coverage of the Andritz and RAG Austria project. Andritz has scheduled an Analyst and Investor Day that is expected to outline corporate strategy for long term profitable growth and explain how sector trends create opportunities across its portfolio. Source: Key Developments. UPM and Andritz have signed a multi year cooperation agreement that gives tissue manufacturers access to the PrimeLineTIAC Tissue Innovation and Application Center in Graz, Austria to develop and optimize next generation tissue products and processes. Source: Key Developments. As part of the UPM and Andritz agreement, UPM hardwood pulp UPM Euca will be the standard pulp for all trials at PrimeLineTIAC, and tissue producers can join joint trials with UPM and Andritz experts to work on efficiency and product performance across dry crepe, textured and structured tissue technologies. Source: Key Developments. Valuation Changes for Andritz Fair Value has risen slightly from €82.83 to €87.33, which brings it closer to the recent price target cluster around €87 to €90. Discount Rate has fallen slightly from 7.64% to 7.31%, which lifts the present value output of the valuation models for Andritz. Revenue Growth is broadly unchanged, moving from 6.25% to 6.27%, so the valuation shift for Andritz is not driven by a major change in top line assumptions. Net Profit Margin has risen modestly from 6.80% to 7.11%, which supports a higher earnings base in the updated Andritz models. Future P/E has fallen slightly from 16.15x to 15.64x, which means the updated fair value for Andritz assumes a marginally lower earnings multiple than before. 36 Set Fair Value 0 votes Share Have other thoughts on Andritz ?
